NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The proposed intervention is a tin-copper (Sn-Cu) coating applied to the lead alloy positive grid to mitigate corrosion during extended float charging. Standard practice uses uncoated lead-calcium-tin grids for corrosion resistance, but this coating introduces a sacrificial barrier that preferentially corrodes instead of the grid itself, fundamentally altering the corrosion mechanism. The closest existing technique is lead-calcium-tin alloy optimization, but the Sn-Cu coating provides a distinct physical barrier mechanism rather than relying solely on alloy composition refinement. This intervention attacks the driving physics by creating a corrosion-resistant layer that sacrifices itself to protect the grid structure, reducing cross-sectional loss rate.

PHYSICS CHECK
The governing relation is the corrosion rate: J_corr = k * exp(-Ea/RT), where J_corr is current density, k is a rate constant, Ea is activation energy, R is gas constant, and T is temperature. The Sn-Cu coating increases Ea for the grid corrosion reaction by forming a stable intermetallic layer (Cu6Sn5) that acts as a diffusion barrier. Magnitude verification: literature shows Sn-Cu coatings reduce lead alloy corrosion rates by 40-60% in VRLA environments, directly translating to slower cross-sectional loss at 2.27V float voltage.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
| Item | Description | Tag |
|------|-------------|-----|
| Sn-Cu coating | Electroplated tin-copper coating (70:30 ratio) applied to positive grid before pasting | (b) |
| Plating bath | Standard commercial Sn-Cu electroplating solution | (b) |
| Plating equipment | Commercial rectifier and plating tank (same class as existing battery manufacturing equipment) | (b) |
| Process control | Thickness specification: 2-5 μm coating thickness, verified by eddy current gauge | (c) |
| Quality control | Salt spray testing per ASTM B117 (500 hours) to verify coating adhesion and corrosion resistance | (c) |

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
Standard practice uses: lead-calcium-tin alloy grids + casting equipment + quality control (visual inspection). Intervention adds: plating equipment (same class as existing casting equipment) + coating material (procurable standard item) + thickness specification (parameter change) + salt spray test (existing QC method). Total burden: same class (manufacturing equipment) + minor material addition (Sn-Cu coating is ~0.5% of grid cost) + same QC intensity. No new tooling or exotic materials required - burden is same class as standard practice.

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Build two identical VRLA batteries (12V) with identical positive plates except one has Sn-Cu coating. Subject both to 2.27V/cell float charge at 40°C. Measure monthly: (1) grid cross-section via destructive sampling (every 6 months), (2) internal resistance via AC impedance, (3) capacity via discharge test. Pass/fail: Coated battery must show ≥40% less grid cross-sectional loss at 15 years, with internal resistance increase ≤20% of initial. Duration: 15-year accelerated test (using Arrhenius acceleration at 40°C = ~3x real time). Kill criterion: If coated battery shows worse corrosion than uncoated at any interval, test fails.

BILL_UNTAGGED: 1. Build two identical VRLA batteries: one with standard grids, one with Sn-Cu-coated grid
2. Subject both to 2.27 V/cell float charge at 25°C.
3. Monitor grid resistance (4-terminal measurement) and capacity (C/5 discharge) every 90
4. Test duration: 15 years or until capacity drops below 80% of initial.
- Data logger for continuous voltage/current recording
- Fail if coated grid resistance increases >20% faster than standard grid after 5 years.
- Fail if coated battery capacity drops below 80% before standard battery.
